source_review.limitations: The attack assumes that a request path can reach the relevant StaticFiles handler without a proxy rewriting away traversal segments and that a readable same-prefix sibling file exists. The patch itself does not establish real deployment disclosure.

Flag a credible file disclosure risk and upgrade; verify the exact raw routing path and file permissions before claiming a specific secret was read.

source_review.fix_review: The repair converts configured removal names to lowercase and compares each supplied header key using lowercase before deleting matching credentials when a redirect changes host.
source_review.regression_evidence: The added dummy-server tests send lowercase authorization to an alternate redirect destination and check it is absent, while testing configurable custom secret removal behavior.
source_review.limitations: Cross-origin redirect behavior, direct caller-specified sensitive header casing, and redirect-removal policy all matter. Disabling removal or not following redirects changes the scenario; successful redirection alone is not proof that valid credentials leaked.

cases.finding_answer: This historical redirect implementation strips sensitive headers using case-sensitive keys. Here a caller supplies a lowercase authorization header and follows a redirect to a different origin under the default removal policy. Flag a credible credential-forwarding risk, reproduce the receiving request safely and upgrade. Do not claim that all redirect requests disclose credentials regardless of header casing.
cases.conditional_answer: The historical code can mishandle differently cased authorization headers on cross-host redirects, but this caller disables automatic redirect following and handles any target change manually. The provided trace contains no cross-host second request, so it does not demonstrate credential forwarding. Recommend a patched dependency and explicit redirect policy without asserting that credentials already reached another host.

source_review.fix_review: The upstream fix replaces recursive formatting with a single match of the numeric prefix and reverse grouping, then appends the untouched suffix to avoid repeated recursive processing.
source_review.regression_evidence: The upstream humanize test expansion adds long and signed numeric formatting cases as well as other expected outputs to protect number formatting behavior.
source_review.limitations: A denial-of-service risk requires sufficiently large attacker-controlled numeric input to reach a template or other callable application path using intcomma without effective length bounds. Small validated numeric strings do not establish the same resource behavior.

cases.finding_answer: The historical intcomma implementation recursively formats long digit strings. This service renders unbounded, untrusted numeric text through that filter, creating a credible resource exhaustion and availability risk. Flag the risky input path, enforce a strict input-length bound and apply the patched Django version. A code weakness is not itself evidence that the service has already exhausted resources.

This route cannot currently supply the oversized digit strings required for the published denial-of-service condition. Recommend patching and maintaining those limits, while avoiding a claim that ordinary short numbers demonstrate a remotely exploitable outage.

source_review.code_boundary: The historical Express res.location code encoded redirect values and included earlier parsing-based checks; malformed URLs could be interpreted inconsistently by URL allowlist checks and Location header handling.
source_review.fix_review: The improved 4.19.2 source patch replaces the earlier host comparison approach with a more direct authority-prefix rule and carefully handles malformed redirect representations; this is not the first attempted fix.
source_review.regression_evidence: The upstream modified test suite contains additional malformed redirect and URI cases, with removed tests from the interim version and new expected behavior, making the improved patch itself the relevant reference.
source_review.limitations: A real open redirect requires an application that accepts user-controlled redirect destinations and an allowlist or validation step that can be bypassed. A hardcoded internal Location value or strictly server-constructed relative path does not demonstrate the advisory.

cases.finding_answer: The historical Express response helper can encode malformed redirect URLs in ways that undermine an application host allowlist. This endpoint accepts user-controlled destinations and validates them before sending the value through res.location. Flag the risk of a redirect escaping the intended host restrictions, upgrade to the fully corrected version and test malformed values without assuming every redirect is unsafe.
